claims.claim: The roadmap and the deletion PRD commit to opposite teardown behavior for the same feature: strategy.md states that ordered or automated deletion of ApplicationSet children will not be implemented and that teardown remains a manual operator action performed one Application at a time, while the PRD's goals ship a deletionOrder field whose Reverse value deletes the generated Applications in reverse rollingSync step order automatically, waiting for each to be fully deleted before the next. The appset incident review raises the same disagreement and explicitly declines to decide it, so no owner has been named to retire one of the two commitments before the PRD lands.

The Stable promotion scope call and the parallel-steps enhancement cannot both proceed as written: T-28927 freezes strategy.rollingSync.steps (the matchExpressions list, one match-set per step) as the v1 shape under the argoproj backward-compatibility bar and requires any change to how a step is expressed to land as a new field before Stable rather than as an in-place restructuring after, while T-28755 proposes exactly an in-place restructuring of steps into parallel / parallelGroups entries. T-28927 notes the scope call is not filed against any specific open enhancement, so the enhancement it forbids has not been told.

Parallel progressive sync steps would break the Reverse deletion strategy at its stated premise: the PRD says Reverse depends on rollingSync.steps remaining a strictly sequential list of match groups, one deployed and deleted at a time, and that any change letting a step contain more than one match group evaluated concurrently removes the single ordering Reverse reverses. T-28755's parallel step form puts multiple matchExpressions groups inside one step precisely so they run concurrently, leaving Reverse with no unambiguous last-in-first-out order to derive.

The incident review's interim restriction that hydrator pilot repos must not use progressive sync until there is a debounce forbids the combination T-24578 requests: T-24578 asks for Source Hydrator support on ApplicationSets so that generated Applications are hydrated to git and their destroy order controlled across ApplicationSets, which is hydrator and progressive-sync-managed ApplicationSets on the same repo. The restriction was written against the pilot ticket, not against T-24578, so this request is scheduled as if the restriction did not exist.

The same hydrator-plus-progressive-sync restriction also blocks T-24417: its motivation for adding Chart to the DrySource spec is that going through helm dependencies makes it difficult to use with ApplicationSets to control chart version across environments, so the feature's stated payoff is hydrator DrySources feeding ApplicationSet-managed applications. While the no-progressive-sync-on-hydrator-pilot rule stands, the use case that justifies the work cannot be exercised on a pilot repo, and nobody has been named to reconcile the two.

The restriction removes the only environment where the Stable-blocking bug reproduces. T-27949's spec-only RollingSync miss is observed on a repository piloting the source hydrator, where every hydration cycle lands a fresh commit picked up as a source change, and the ticket admits there is no counter incrementing when specChanged fires without a resulting sync operation, so the 1-in-6 figure is a count of support pings rather than a measured rate. Forbidding progressive sync on hydrator pilot repos until a debounce exists takes that fleet out of service, leaving the bug both unmeasured and no longer reproducible where it was seen.

The sharding date rests on a close condition nobody has bounded. strategy.md commits this quarter's application controller capacity to the Progressive Sync Stable punch list and states sharding will not start until the Stable promotion closes, with the same pair owning both. T-28927 defines that punch list only as two open backlog queries plus a scope call that is not filed against any specific enhancement, so the gating list has no enumerated membership and the sharding start date inherits that indeterminacy.

The platform sync call's decision that impersonation goes behind a per-project flag and that nobody flips it on a project until the diff story is fixed blocks T-27833's only proposed remedy: T-27833 proposes using the service account impersonation feature with a split between resources handled by the Argo CD control plane and resources handled by the impersonated SA, so that the impersonated SA loses permission on kind: Namespace. That work cannot be piloted on any project while the flag freeze stands, and the freeze is recorded only in the sync call notes, not on the ticket.

The impersonation freeze also collides with the fix request that is supposed to lift it. T-28695 asks that Server-Side Diff run as the same identity as sync by honoring the AppProject's destinationServiceAccounts, and its reproduction requires application.sync.impersonation.enabled together with controller.diff.server.side on real external clusters. The freeze forbids enabling impersonation on a project until the diff story is fixed, so the diff fix cannot be validated in the configuration it is written for, and T-28695 additionally warns that #24134 making Server Side Diff the default would push every external-cluster user into that same combination on upgrade.

Deprioritizing hydrator rollback while signing advances leaves a gap with no named owner. Note-1 moves T-27327 to next quarter and reassigns the dev pair to the progressive sync deletion loop, while T-28239 proposes commit-server GPG signing whose public key the operator adds to the project's SourceIntegrity policy. T-27327 states that rollback pushes happen outside the commit server, so once SourceIntegrity requires verified signatures the rollback commit lands unsigned and the git host rejects the push, with no messaging tying the failure to signing and no retry path from the History and Rollback tab. Enabling signing therefore depends on work that has been pushed out of the quarter.

A cross-team dependency of the hydrator design is owned by nobody and is already producing bugs. RFC-002 makes push-to-stage a mode whose whole point is to be an integration point for an external promotion system, and explicitly lists implementing a change promotion system as a non-goal. T-26443's stale-manifest auto-sync is observed only in push-to-stage mode, precisely because the external promoter has not yet moved fresh manifests to the deployment branch. Note-1 records that this promoter is still a shell script that nobody owns, and parks the question.

The root cause of T-26271 was settled in one team and never delivered to the team still chasing it. The sync call root-caused the CI diff failures to impersonation being on, which makes diff run as the destination service account that lacks patch on cluster-scoped resources, and left the writeup to an unnamed someone. T-26271 still reads as an unexplained narrowing, with the reporter noting the failing jobs are in projects where the sync impersonation flag was recently enabled and that they do not understand why the diff runs with a narrower identity than the broad cluster Secret.
